patch_description: The current enhanced filter is a plain exponentially-weighted moving average. A weighted moving average is biased whenever the signal has a slope: it lags behind trends, which hurts lag_error, accuracy, and tracking. A better approach is a *weighted local linear (degree-1) regression* over each window, evaluated at the most recent sample (the window end). This is zero-lag with respect to linear trends: fitting y ≈ a·t + b over the window and evaluating at the last sample removes the systematic trend-induced bias of a moving average, while the exponential weights still emphasize recent samples for adaptivity to non-stationarity. Additionally, a single Huber-style robust reweighting pass downweights outlier samples within the window, suppressing noise spikes that cause spurious directional reversals (improving slope_changes and false_reversals). Solving the 2-parameter weighted least squares in closed form is cheap (O(W) per window), preserving the excellent efficiency score. To avoid amplifying noise when the residual scale is tiny or the system is ill-conditioned, we fall back gracefully to the weighted mean.
